title: APAC edge partner capability thermometer and procurement triggers
creator: Rina Patel
description: Synthesize a capability heatmap of APAC edge inference partners (cloud + colo + local integrators) to identify procurement triggers and shortlist 3 candidate partners for pilot Dedicated/Private deployments. Deliverables: 1) partner capability thermometer (latency/cost/availability/model-compat), 2) procurement trigger matrix, 3) recommended pilot partner shortlist and ask list.
background: As Redwood expands Private and Dedicated options into APAC, we need an evidence-driven snapshot of the supply side: who can provide low-latency inference near customer clusters, which model families they can host (quantized/INT8/FP16), and what procurement thresholds (SLA, capacity commit, price bands) should trigger negotiations. Existing model-scout docs cover model features but not partner operational readiness for edge/regional capacity.
objectives: Map 12 potential APAC partners across 6 capability dimensions (latency, throughput, model coverage, security/compliance, deployment flexibility, pricing transparency)
Define 4 procurement triggers that should move a prospective partner from 'monitor' to 'pilot' to 'commit'
Produce a one-page partner heatmap + a two-page procurement ask template for sales/partnerships
scope_inclusions: Cloud providers with APAC regions, local colo providers, managed inference partners, systems integrators with on-prem capabilities
Model-compatibility (LLM families we currently vet: Llama-like, Mistral, Vicuna-derived, LLMs with 16k+ context support)
Latency percentiles from partner test endpoints where available
scope_exclusions: Pure academic/research groups without commercial SLAs
GPU hardware resellers that don't operate inference stacks
Edge IoT device vendors outside of colocated inference
hypothesis: At least 60% of candidate partners will support one of our prioritized open-model families but only ~25% will meet <50ms p95 latency to key APAC metros without an initial committed capacity contract.
research_methodology: Synthetic latency/throughput probes to publicly-exposed endpoints and partner trial accounts
30-min discovery interviews with partner ops/solutions engineers
data_sources: Public endpoints for latency testing (various partner URLs) - see testsheet
Redwood console usage telemetry for APAC trials (internal dashboard link) - https://console.redwood-internal/reports/apac-telemetry
competitive_signals_found: Several smaller managed-hosting partners advertise support for 8-bit quantized runtime but lack transparent throughput benchmarks
One regional cloud partner offers a consumption-based Dedicated-like tier with 99.9% SLA but requires 3-month minimum commitment
Two systems integrators can do air-gapped installs but require hardware procurement lead times of 8-12 weeks
Price per vGPU-hour ranges widely (USD 0.8 - 3.6) for comparable T4/A10p class instances when billed monthly
implications: We should treat model-compatibility claims as 'claims' until validated via test probes; allocate two engineering smoke-test days per shortlisted partner
Procurement triggers must include hardware lead time and commit length to avoid operational surprises
Fallback routing strategies will be necessary in metros where partners cannot deliver low p95 latency without committed capacity
recommended_actions: Send RFI to top-12 partners this week using the attached RFI template
Perform a 48-hour synthetic probe sweep of partner test endpoints to measure p50/p95 latency and cold-start behavior
Create pilot SOW template that defaults to a 30-day low-commit window for latency-sensitive customers
Prioritize partners who publish kernel/runtime tuning guidance or provide RH-compatible containers for quicker onboarding
acceptance_criteria: Heatmap covering at least 10 partners with normalized scores across 6 dimensions
Procurement trigger matrix with at least 4 measurable triggers (latency p95, minimum commit, security posture, lead time)
Pilot shortlist (3 partners) with clear 'ask' per partner and red/yellow/green readiness status
risks: Partners may not share meaningful throughput numbers without an NDA
Latency probes against public endpoints may not reflect real-production behavior behind private links
Lead-time uncertainty for on-prem installs could push pilots beyond Q2 timeline
decisions: Scope will be limited to partners with commercial presence in at least one APAC metro (Singapore, Sydney, Tokyo, Seoul, Mumbai)
We will not pursue air-gapped pilots in this cycle unless partner can commit to <6 week hardware lead time
notes: Initial list of 18 partners compiled from channel team + marketplace scans; plan to cull to top 12 for RFI
Sales flagged two enterprise prospects requiring Singapore-local inference with <40ms p95 as a near-term blocker
Budget estimate: $12k for partner trials including short-term cloud commitments and test instances
